reason: Replace and de-authorize Yance-owned production provider-gateway and physical model-routing infrastructure with mature OSS LiteLLM v1.95.0 base SDK Router/ComplexityRouter as the Model Brain production authority. Yance remains responsible only for product-specific task/context/privacy/capability projection, credential authority, catalog/capability discovery without model ranking, queue/cancellation/stale-result fencing, signed execution evidence, user settings and final reply/send authority. LiteLLM must own provider normalization, streaming, retry/fallback, cooldown/load balancing, runtime health/availability handling, provider selection, token/cost normalization and physical model selection. LiteLLM may not be placed behind the legacy Yance router or a Yance pre-routing model shortlist and no second Yance Model Gateway or Router is authorized.

supersedesProposal.reason: Independent review found that the proposal branch history contained transient out-of-scope noop/tmp commits and that hard-tag AND/fail-closed plus persistent-child credential transport semantics needed to be frozen before authorization merge. This clean replacement is created from trusted main without history rewrite.

digestCanonicalization.canonicalText: Join the normalized sorted unique path list with LF and append exactly one trailing LF before hashing. This is the workPackageChangedFilesSha256 contract used by shared/release/implementationBranchPolicy.js.

liteLLM.integration: Adopt the exact MIT litellm/ source tree plus dependency versions/hashes from the exact upstream uv.lock. Use LiteLLM Router, strict tag filtering and ComplexityRouter directly as production gateway/routing authority; do not fork or copy the routing engine.

uv.role: Reuse the already-reviewed Yance build/sealing-time uv input; it must not be required at application runtime.

pythonBuildStandalone.role: Reuse the already-reviewed standalone CPython runtime supply-chain input for the sealed Windows Model Brain runtime.

routingOssFitDecision.productionAuthority: LiteLLM v1.95.0 base SDK Router + strict tag filtering + ComplexityRouter; AdaptiveRouter may be enabled only through the same pinned LiteLLM source when tests prove the configured policy.

routeLLM.reason: No official release/tag lifecycle and stale maintenance relative to current 2026 Model Brain production requirements. Mature OSS mandatory adoption does not require mechanically adopting an obsolete named upstream.

aurelioSemanticRouter.reason: Actively maintained and LiteLLM-compatible, but LiteLLM v1.95.0 already supplies the required complexity/adaptive/tag routing authority. Adding a second router would create unnecessary dependency and authority duplication.

vllmSemanticRouter.reason: Capable and active, but its local service/runtime model is materially heavier for native Windows/offline Yance P0 and is unnecessary while pinned LiteLLM already satisfies the routing contract.

hardEligibilityAndTagPolicy.reason: Pinned LiteLLM Router defaults tag_filtering_match_any to true and its tag router may use deployments tagged default when a tagged request has no direct match. Yance hard requirements require all mandatory tags to hold simultaneously and must never fall back to a deployment that did not satisfy them.

openCoreBoundary.rootLicenseRule: enterprise/ is separately licensed; content outside enterprise/ is MIT under the pinned root LICENSE.
openCoreBoundary.nativeBridgePolicy: Do not compile or require the litellm-rust workspace for this P0. The pinned LiteLLM Python core has an official fallback when the optional _native bridge is absent; tests must prove the selected Router/provider paths work without it.
openCoreBoundary.dependencyMaterialization: Use the exact upstream uv.lock as dependency version/hash authority. Materialize only the base SDK dependency closure: no proxy extra, no enterprise distribution, no dev dependency group, no workspace member installation/emission and no root project installation. Then place only the exact litellm/ Git tree into the sealed runtime. Runtime dependency resolution is forbidden.

legacyRetirement.deletionFollowUpAllowed: Dead legacy files may be physically deleted in this exact package only if already inside the authorized path set; otherwise deletion requires a separately authorized cleanup package. Their continued presence must not imply runtime authority.

runtimeBoundary.childOwns: pinned LiteLLM Router instances and provider calls only

routingSignals.projectionMechanism: logical model group plus LiteLLM deployment tags/metadata and request metadata. Mandatory hard tags use AND semantics. Yance must not score/rank physical providers after projection and must not project transient provider health/cooldown state. Legacy OpenRouter selectionScore/qualityTier/usagePolicy/preferredRoute/frontier scores are explicitly forbidden as production routing inputs.

mandatoryFailureFirstContracts: The first implementation commit contains tests only. Before product code, those tests must produce a causal RED because the pinned LiteLLM runtime/integration is absent and legacy Yance routing/direct-provider execution is still authoritative.

No production inference may select champion, primary, fallback, emergency, provider or model in Yance before entering LiteLLM. Physical model/provider selection must be proven to originate from the pinned LiteLLM Router result.

Production aiGateway execution must call modelBrainRuntime directly and must not call legacy modelExecutionHost/startModelExecution, aiQualityRouteAuthority.routePlan/classifyFailure, workload placement, provider failure-domain, Yance budget routing or model service task-routing authorities to choose/retry/fallback a physical model.

The production JobQueue providerKey must not be derived from a preselected physical provider/model; queueing must remain logical Model Brain work while LiteLLM owns physical provider concurrency/routing.
modelExecutor must not perform a direct provider switch to ollamaClient/openAiCompatibleClient for model inference; qualification and benchmark calls must traverse LiteLLM too.
mediaIntelligenceService image/video representative-frame model inference must traverse Model Brain/LiteLLM and must not call ollamaClient directly.
bilingualUnderstandingService must not call aiGateway.resolveRoute to preselect a translation model; translation must use the logical group/tags path into LiteLLM.

modelAutoActivationService and modelRegistry qualification/benchmark/startup repair flows must not auto-write or rebalance authoritative primary/fallback physical routes even when legacy callers pass autoSelectVerified/rebalance options.

openRouterAutoConfigurationService must retain only account/catalog/capability discovery and deterministic non-ranking registration. familyQuality, qualityTier, usagePolicy, roleScore, rankForRole, buildSelections, frontier preferredRoute and equivalent Yance model-ranking outputs must not influence the production deployment pool or routing order.
No usable sealed Model Brain runtime is an explicit fail-closed/degraded RED for AI inference; legacy direct provider clients must never become fallback authority.

LiteLLM Router must run with enable_tag_filtering=true and tag_filtering_match_any=false for mandatory hard-eligibility tags. A mandatory-tag request must never use a default deployment fallback, and no deployment satisfying every mandatory tag must fail closed.

The pinned LiteLLM ComplexityRouter must be the complexity-tier classifier/routing implementation when complexity routing is enabled; no copied or rewritten Yance complexity scoring engine is allowed.
Provider retry/fallback/cooldown/load balancing/rate-limit/runtime health handling must be performed by LiteLLM rather than duplicate Yance loops.

Successful result evidence must bind the selected physical model to LiteLLM model_id/result metadata and bind token/cost metrics to LiteLLM/provider-normalized result data; Yance catalog cost estimation must not be production cost authority.

Provider secrets must enter the persistent Model Brain child only over the private stdio in-memory protocol; provider secrets in child environment, command line, logs, renderer state, persistent state, receipts, SBOM or provenance are RED.

The shipped runtime contains only the pinned MIT litellm/ upstream source tree and the base SDK dependency closure; enterprise/, litellm-proxy-extras/, proxy extras, dev groups and workspace projects are absent.
The runtime must not require LiteLLM Proxy Server, litellm[proxy], litellm-enterprise, a Rust toolchain, pip, uv, Git, system Python or online dependency resolution at application startup.

Windows x64 sealed runtime must be built from the exact pinned upstream/source/lock/tool/runtime inputs and pass offline import, Router construction, strict tag-routing, complexity-routing and health closure with build tools absent from the shipped runtime.
Deterministic CycloneDX 1.7 runtime SBOM plus upstream provenance/license/tree evidence must be generated and verified before GREEN.
Letta, Graphiti, Parlant, Persona, Learning Brain, Voice, Facebook and Presence authorities remain unchanged and are not implemented or modified by this work package.
